sections.name: File setup, BUCKETS
sections.title: Imports and timing bucket order
sections.what: Brings in the chart parts, helpers, shared tiles and panels, and fixes the order of the seven completion timing buckets, from the nearest term through to unknown.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed order keeps the timing bars in the same sequence every time.
sections.watch_out: A new bucket must be added here and also given a label and a bar color rule in the timing section, or it will show without a label or in the wrong color.

sections.name: SummaryView (part 1)
sections.title: Headline numbers and capex by phase
sections.what: Works out totals and groups for countries, phases, industries, companies and timing. Draws four headline tiles and a horizontal bar chart of capex by lifecycle phase, with a row of links below to each phase's projects.
sections.why: Likely reason: headline tiles that also state how many projects report a value let the reader judge how complete the totals are.
sections.watch_out: The bar chart keeps only phases with a capex figure, so a phase with no capex never appears as a bar, though it still appears as a link below.

sections.name: SummaryView (part 2)
sections.title: Timing, top countries and top companies
sections.what: Draws the completion timing bars with counts and a link to the forecast. Draws the top ten countries with project counts and capex, and the top ten companies with project counts and capex coverage.
sections.why: Likely reason: ranked tables show the largest contributors first.
sections.watch_out: Countries and companies are cut to ten. A project with no country is left out of the country table but still counted in the headline.

sections.name: SummaryView (part 3)
sections.title: Industry mix tiles
sections.what: On the all-industries page with more than one industry, draws one tile per industry showing its project count and capex coverage, each linking to that industry's dataset.
sections.why: Likely reason: a cross-industry comparison is only useful when several industries are shown, so it is hidden on a single-industry page.
sections.watch_out: These tiles appear only when more than one industry exists, so the layout changes with the data.

summary: The overview dashboard for the portfolio, showing headline numbers, capex by phase, completion timing, top countries, top companies and industry mix.
purpose: Gives a quick picture of the portfolio and links each figure to the detail view where it can be explored.
why: Likely reason: a summary first, with links into detail, lets a reader orient before digging into individual projects.
how: Works out totals from the projects, then groups them by country, phase, industry and company. Buckets projects by completion timing. Draws four headline tiles, a bar chart of capex by phase with links into the dataset, a timing bar list with a link to the forecast, a table of the top ten countries, a list of the top companies, and industry tiles when not on a single-industry page.
inputs: The list of projects, the industry name lookup, and the web address state for the current scope and link building.
outputs: The dashboard on screen. Clicking any figure opens a view with matching filters. Nothing is saved.
risks: Total capex only adds projects that report a value, so the total can be partial; the card shows how many projects report. Top lists are cut to ten or eight entries, hiding the rest. Phase colors are assigned from the phases present, so the same phase may change color in a different scope.
debug: If a total looks wrong, compare the note under the card that shows how many projects report capex. If a phase bar is missing, check whether that phase has any capex values, since only those phases are charted. If a link opens the wrong filter, check the link parameters for that item. If timing counts do not add up, check the timing bucket helper in the portfolio library.
